definition: Opening setup is the first transfer after an in-bounds pull is caught or picked up, when that transfer hands the disc to the player who starts the offense. It need not move toward the middle. If the pull receiver attacks directly, including when the defense prevents an opening transfer, recorded throw 1 is already attacking. After one confirmed setup transfer, all later passes count as attacking, including handler weaves, resets, and passes to an open handler. For a confirmed brick or sideline restart, or a later possession after a turnover, count the first pass as attacking. Bringing a turnover to the goal line or tapping it in does not create a pull setup. A failed setup attempt remains a turnover in the full-possession record; it can have zero attacking throws. Caught-versus-grounded pull handling may be unclear even when setup is clear. A penalty before the first brick-start pass does not turn that pass into setup. Use an uncertain label when the film does not settle the distinction. Opening setup is a working expectation with explicit exceptions, not a reason to remove every opening pass automatically.

timeoutPolicy.status: Adopted by user on 2026-11-12; full-cohort implementation pending
timeoutPolicy.unit: The original receiving-point lineup, followed across its offensive possessions.
timeoutPolicy.rule: Keep completed possessions before a timeout substitution changes the original lineup. Exclude possessions played by replacement players from the original-line comparison; label them not applicable because of substitution, never zero or unsuccessful.
timeoutPolicy.completedBeforeChange: Keep physical throws, identified attacking throws, hucks and the observed goal or turnover from each completed original-line possession.
timeoutPolicy.interruptedPossession: If the lineup changes during a possession, preserve the earlier actions as a partial record. Do not treat that partial record as a completed possession, use it in mean completed-possession length or scoring rate, or attach a later lineup’s goal/turnover to it.
timeoutPolicy.unresolvedOutcome: An eventual hold, break or defensive recovery resolved after the original players are replaced is not applicable to the original-line outcome analysis. Do not recode it as a failed recovery or a break. Preserve the actual receiving-team outcome in the source record.
timeoutPolicy.timeoutWithoutSubstitution: A timeout alone does not establish a new lineup. Flag it separately because rest or tactical changes can still affect behavior; do not silently equate it with a replacement line.
timeoutPolicy.partialSubstitution: For the primary comparison, use the conservative implementation of the same original seven. Flag any recorded substitution, including partial changes. Stop the original-line sequence at its first lineup change; do not resume it by renumbering later possessions.
timeoutPolicy.unknownLineup: Unknown personnel remain unverified; do not assume the original seven continued.
timeoutPolicy.reporting: Report retained complete possessions, interrupted partial possessions and excluded later possessions separately. Explain that later-possession results apply only to original groups that recover the disc and remain on the field.
